extracted.intended_audience: authors, reviewers, and editors submitting to or working with PeerJ journals
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedures for preparing, submitting, reviewing, and publishing manuscripts in PeerJ journals, including ethical, data-sharing, authorship, and taxonomic requirements. Applies to authors, reviewers, and editors involved in PeerJ submission workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Access license (CC BY)
rubrics_metrics.description: All PeerJ articles are published under a Creative Commons Attribution License; authors retain copyright but allow sharing, adaptation and commercial use provided appropriate attribution is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure any copyrighted material included is also available under a similarly liberal license; the CC BY licensing meets or exceeds funder/institutional open access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: PeerJ account and co-author confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: The submitting author must have created a free PeerJ account at submission; co-authors receive an email after submission with directions to confirm co-authorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam folders for PeerJ emails and add [email protected] to contact lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication payment options and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance and before production, authors must decide how to pay: (1) PeerJ Individual Lifetime Memberships, (2) a single article processing charge (APC), or (3) apply for institutional fee assistance if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If >12 authors only 12 need lifetime memberships; remaining authors must have at least a free account. Authors can pay up to editorial acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver policies (country and undergraduate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors from World Bank Low-income economies can request a waiver for one publication per submitting author per year; undergraduate co-authors may request a one-time waiver if senior co-authors hold paid Individual Lifetime Memberships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests and reasons should be indicated in the 'Confidential Notes to Staff' at submission; editors/reviewers are not informed of waiver requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Admin responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Submission Admin must inform all co-authors of submission, ensure manuscript adherence to all journal policies (publication ethics, data/materials deposition, etc.), manage correspondence, designate a substitute, ensure co-authors have publishing plans or responsibility for charges, create the submission themselves (not an external agency), ensure manuscript is free from spelling/grammatical/unclear expression, and ensure author names entered online exactly match the Author Cover Page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are required duties; submission may be held up or returned if not met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication Corresponding Author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the proofing PDF and respond to production queries; post-publication, respond to queries and provide data/materials as requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corresponding author remains point of contact for production and post-publication issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorship credit should be based on: (1) substantial contributions to conception/design, data acquisition, or analysis/interpretation; (2) drafting the article or critical revision for important intellectual content; and (3) final approval of the version to be published. Authors should meet conditions 1, 2, and 3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acquisition of funding, data collection, or general supervision alone does not constitute authorship. All persons designated as authors should qualify and all who qualify should be listed. Each author should be able to take public responsibility for appropriate portions of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group authorship naming and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: When a large multicenter group has conducted the work, identify individuals who accept direct responsibility for the manuscript; these individuals should meet full authorship criteria and be named individually in the byline; the formal group name should be listed last.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List other members in Acknowledgments. NLM indexes the group name and the individuals identified as responsible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author name change policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ will change an author's name on request with as few barriers as possible; no reason or proof is required. Names will be changed online and in PDFs and publications will be republished with the same DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests should come from the author and be sent in confidence to [email protected]; PeerJ follows COPE best practices and will not publicise the change unless asked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author type limits (corresponding, submission admins, equal first authors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to two authors can be designated Corresponding Authors; up to two Submission Admins; up to two Equal First Authors (first and second, or first and last).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow these limits when completing submission metadata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ keeps all details about submitted manuscripts confidential, does not publicly comment about submitted or rejected manuscripts, and maintains reviewer confidentiality unless permission to reveal identities is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors, reviewers and editors must treat correspondence as confidential unless explicitly stated otherwise. PeerJ may share materials with relevant parties during misconduct investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model (single-anonymized)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are subject to initial appraisal and, if suitable, to single anonymized peer review by independent expert referees (reviewer identity hidden from authors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows STM definitions; reviewers may opt to reveal their identities to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity transparency and published review information
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer identity is not made visible to author by default; author identity is visible to reviewer; reviewer and author identity are visible to the decision-making editor. Review reports, the submitted manuscript, author/editor communication (decision letters and reviewer responses) are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer identities will be published only if reviewers opt in; identities of handling editors are published. For submissions created before 13 Feb 2023, authors could opt out of publishing peer review history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-publication commenting openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-publication commenting is open to anybody; comments can be anonymous, require signing in, or require registration depending on settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenting settings are applied by the journal/platform and must follow commenting policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to publication ethics and COPE procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ adheres to prevailing industry standards (COPE, CSE, WAME) for investigating publication ethics and follows COPE Code of Conduct and Best Practice Guidelines when issues are raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ will follow recommended COPE procedures during investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of specific misconducts
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ does not tolerate dual publication, dual submission, plagiarism, data/figure fabrication or manipulation, knowingly providing incorrect information, copyright infringement, inaccurate author attributions, attempts to manipulate peer review, unethical citation practices (including excessive self-citation or citation of nonexistent/irrelevant sources), use of generative AI without clear attribution, failures to declare conflicts of interest, fraud, and libel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If uncertain about what constitutes such actions consult COPE/CSE/WAME resources. PeerJ will rigorously enforce standards and may report individuals or retract manuscripts in extreme cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy on generative AI and AI-assisted technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Generative AI-assisted technologies (LLMs, image generators) cannot be listed as authors. AI-generated data, images, and reference lists are strictly prohibited (except as the subject of the work). Authors must disclose any use of AI tools at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI is used in research, authors must provide comprehensive information in Methods including tool/version and full prompts. AI used purely for editing (typos/language) should be acknowledged in Acknowledgments. Undeclared or hidden AI use is a serious breach and may lead to rejection or other actions. PeerJ reserves editorial discretion to decline manuscripts where AI compromises integrity or authorship contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties (authors, reviewers, academic editors) must transparently declare any potential competing interests. Disclosure does not necessarily imply a problem but provides transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors declare upon submission; reviewers consider competing interests before agreeing and confirm none before submitting a review; editors should recuse themselves if they feel they have a competing interest. Potential interests should be declared even if the individual feels they are not actual conflicts. Examples include financial benefits, personal/working relationships with authors, patent activity, consultancy, gifts, personal convictions. Undisclosed competing interests may lead to cancellation of review, removal of individuals, or retraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on reviewer self-citation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a potential competing interest for any reviewer to suggest a citation to their own work as part of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When suggesting a self-citation reviewers must (1) declare this as a potential competing interest and (2) provide clear justification in their review as to why the citation is relevant to the study. Authors should include additional references suggested during peer review only if they agree they are relevant and useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must disclose the financing which made their work possible; the Funding statement is published in the final article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate from competing interests; provide full funding sources and grant numbers where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics statement and approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Where applicable, authors must provide an Ethics statement detailing relevant ethical standards met. Ethics statements are required for research including human participants, human tissue, or regulated animals (vertebrates or cephalopods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide ethics statement upon submission and include full information in Materials and Methods (name of granting organization and approval reference numbers). If no approval reference number, provide written approval as a confidential supplemental file. For verbal consent used in recordings, ensure IRB-approved procedures or provide proof if consent was waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field research permits and permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When research is conducted outside institutional or permanent field stations, appropriate permission/field research permits to access the site must have been obtained per applicable laws and norms; adequate proof must be provided at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If verbal permission was obtained provide the name and authority of the person. Provide collection permits for samples and export documentation if materials were exported. Consider privacy/animal welfare issues with camera traps/drones and operate UAVs in accordance with regulations. Documentation may be requested in confidence and is not necessarily published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual Use Research of Concern (definition and reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dual Use Research of Concern is life-sciences research that could be reasonably anticipated to be misapplied to pose significant threats to public health, agriculture, environment, materiel, or national security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ reserves the right to consider submissions sensitive on a case-by-case basis; authors, editors, or reviewers should report concerns to staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data, materials, code and protocol availability at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must make materials, code, data, and associated protocols available at the time of submission for peer review and publication; the preferred route is public deposition in appropriate repositories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance will be investigated and may lead to actions by PeerJ. FORCE11 recommendations and domain-specific guidelines should be followed. Provide accession numbers/DOIs and metadata; deposit raw reads and assembled sequences in appropriate archives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository deposition and accession numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Large domain-specific datasets should be deposited in public repositories (e.g., GenBank, PDB, PRIDE, Addgene, etc.) and accession numbers or access addresses provided in the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult re3data.org, FAIRSharing.org or NIH repository lists for repositories. If no suitable repository exists, supporting datasets may be included as Supplemental Information files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-readable data formats and acceptable file types
rubrics_metrics.description: Data should be provided in appropriate, machine-readable formats; PDF, PowerPoint, and images of tables are not acceptable for raw data sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare raw data in standard formats and provide metadata to enhance discoverability (ontology terms etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical materials deposition and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Physical materials (type specimens, microbial isolates, mutant seed stock, voucher specimens, etc.) must be permanently deposited in recognized centers where appropriate, and accession numbers provided at submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of repositories and culture collections are listed (RIKEN, Jackson Lab, ATCC, Addgene, etc.). For novel research compounds, disclose chemical identity and provide rigorous evidence for purity and identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code availability and archival requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All code needed to reproduce the results, and all raw data, must be made available either in a repository such as GitHub/GitLab (with a DOI via Zenodo) or as a supplementary file published alongside the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party code must be cited appropriately with a DOI or Software Heritage ID. GitHub repositories can be archived by Zenodo; GitLab repositories must be released and archived to obtain a DOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of private/restricted data during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Some repositories offer confidential hosting and anonymous access for reviewers; authors using such services must provide anonymous reviewer access and coordinate prompt public release upon acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any potential restrictions on data/code/materials (proprietary data, human subjects restrictions) must be disclosed at submission, including how other researchers might attempt replication without access. Authors may not be sole contacts for access; data must be submitted to a suitable third party when restrictions apply. PeerJ reserves the right to refuse consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and statistical result standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should adhere to reporting standards of their field, indicate which standards were followed, and provide checklists/protocols as Supplemental Information where appropriate. Statistical results must be reported in full (test performed, reason for choosing test, test statistic, sample size, degrees of freedom, exact p-value to 2 decimal spaces unless p<0.001, or confidence intervals, and effect sizes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply corrections for multiple testing where appropriate. Do not report inferential stats for known quantities; show data distribution (overlay bar graphs with scatter plots, use boxplots/violin plots, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature review standards
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ considers timely, well-balanced literature reviews; recommended maximum ~8,000–12,000 words to keep reviews focused, with a rationale for why needed, intended audience, and description of procedures used to ensure comprehensiveness and lack of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify gaps and future directions. Unbalanced reviews intended to support a particular view will not be considered. Follow standard sections for literature review articles. Scoping reviews are considered if meeting definitions; if review answers a clinically meaningful question it should be submitted as a systematic review/meta-analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registered Reports (Stage 1) consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ will consider Stage 1 Registered Reports which separate review of research question and protocol from results and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See OSF for detailed guidance on Registered Report workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: New species and taxonomic-specific publication requirements (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special requirements apply when naming new species to increase discoverability and to comply with relevant Codes (ICZN, ICN, Bacteriological Code, ICN fungal rules, ICTV, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific sub-requirements for zoological, botanical, fungal, bacterial, viral, and diatom taxa as outlined by PeerJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: New zoological taxonomic names requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To name a new zoological taxon, authors must comply with ICZN rules and register details in ZooBank; include globally unique identifier (LSID) with new species name in metadata and include required Methods section text about PDF representing a published work and ZooBank LSIDs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact ZooBank early to obtain LSIDs; PeerJ is archived in repositories that support ICZN registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: New botanical taxon requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ requires the globally unique identifier (LSID) to be listed under new taxon names in the Results section; PeerJ staff will contact IPNI at acceptance to provide identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must use specific Methods section wording provided by PeerJ; obtaining an LSID isn’t an ICN requirement but is required by PeerJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: New fungal taxon requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For fungi, include an identifier issued by MycoBank or Index Fungorum in the protologue; include a 'Nomenclature' subsection in Methods with the required wording about MycoBank submission and archiving.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MycoBank numbers or equivalent must be included. LSIDs or Globally Unique Identifiers may be required where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: New bacterial taxon requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide evidence that type strains are deposited in two recognized culture collections in two different countries and upload certificates as Supplemental Files; to validate names published outside IJSEM, submit covering letter and copies/PDFs to IJSEM Editorial Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Bacteriological Code requirements for validation lists and deposition documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: New viral taxon requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: New viral taxa must be approved by ICTV before names are official; authors must provide proof that a proposal has been made or accepted to ICTV at submission and appropriately cite the proposal URL and status in metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite ICTV proposal URLs for proposed, approved-but-not-ratified, and approved-and-ratified-but-not-yet-published statuses as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: New diatom taxon recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: For diatom names no formal registration is necessary, but authors are recommended to ensure names are included in DiatomBase and forward PDFs/DOIs to DiatomBase promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DiatomBase is part of WoRMS and can assign LSIDs after publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Critique' submission standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that critique or reanalyse another published article or the work of an individual/group may be considered if they are within scope as a research article and include substantial reanalysis of data or presentation of new data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ policy is to invite the critiqued party to comment as a non-anonymous reviewer and to seek at least two additional reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer and editor opposition requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may request that specific individuals be prevented from seeing their submission (opposition), but such requests should be limited, refer to specific individuals (not broad categories), and be made only with good reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PeerJ will attempt to accommodate reasonable requests but cannot guarantee all will be honoured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals process for editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may appeal decisions by emailing editorial.support@peerj.com; appeals cannot be prioritised over new submissions and may take time. PeerJ aims to respond within two weeks to initial appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals must include detailed reasons why the original decision was in error and a point-by-point response to reviewer/Academic Editor comments. PeerJ may involve the Editorial Board and re-review; the decision resulting from the appeal process is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints, prior non-journal dissemination and embargoes
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ does not accept material previously published in recognized peer-reviewed journals (dual publication) but accepts preprints, conference presentations, and non-journal venues (blogs/posters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors discussing unaccepted submissions should state so and inform editorial office if discussing with journalists. If press released, PeerJ will set an embargo on news coverage corresponding to publication date and requests media respect the embargo. Authors cannot require NDAs preventing journalists from discussing embargoed articles with researchers after press release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting policy for published content
rubrics_metrics.description: All public comments must follow normal standards of professional discourse; commenters are named and associated with PeerJ profiles; anonymous/pseudonymous commenting is not allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters should declare possible conflicts of interest. Insulting, inflammatory, obscene, or libelous language is not tolerated. PeerJ may edit/remove comments to align with policies and remove commenting rights for repeat offenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright permissions for reused material
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ publishes accepted manuscripts under a CC BY license; authors are responsible for obtaining appropriate permissions from original publishers to republish previously published text, figures, tables, Supplementary Information, etc., under CC BY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain and document permissions prior to acceptance/production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction policy
rubrics_metrics.description: PeerJ reserves the right to retract articles found to be fraudulent (e.g., subject to deception such as data manipulation) or in serious breach of policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retractions may follow investigations and COPE-recommended procedures; authors/institutions may be notified or reported as appropriate.
